item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-07 23:59
Institution: ROMA "La Sapienza", Roma
Field: Medicine / 06/MEDS-08 Endocrinologia, nefrologia e scienze dell'alimentazione e del benessere

This project aims to investigate the molecular mechanisms underlying the nephroprotective effects of SGLT2 inhibition, with a focus on the role of the SIRT1/HIF-1α/HIF-2α signaling axis in diabetic nephropathy. The study will explore how empagliflozin (EMPA) modulates the balance between HIF-1α and HIF-2α through SIRT1 activation and how these pathways influence cellular adaptation to metabolic and hypoxic stress.

item.title: Incarico di ricerca: Influence of neuroautonomic modulation on ventricular arrhythmic burden in endurance athletes: a comparison between structurally normal hearts and non-ischemic left ventricular myocardial scar (Univ. PADOVA)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-10-20 13:00
Institution: Univ. PADOVA, Padova
Field: Medicine / 06/MEDS-07 Malattie dell'apparato cardiovascolare e malattie dell'apparato respiratorio

The project will compare approximately 50 athletes with ventricular arrhythmias and non-ischaemic left ventricular myocardial scar, already followed at the Sports Cardiology Clinic of Padua University Hospital, with a prospective cohort of athletes with frequent ventricular arrhythmias but structurally normal hearts. Groups will be matched for age, sex, and sport type. Arrhythmic burden and cardiac autonomic modulation will be assessed through one-week prolonged ECG monitoring, including rest, sleep, and at least three training sessions, with analysis of heart rate variability and fragmentation. Advanced autonomic analysis will be performed in collaboration with the University of Milan.

item.title: Incarico di ricerca: Pica Code IR-2026-081 - Computational Models for new Patients Stratification Strategies of Neuromuscular Disorders. (Univ. MODENA e R. E.)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-10-19 13:00
Institution: Univ. MODENA e R. E., Modena
Field: Medicine / 06/MEDS-01 Genetica medica

The researcher will analyze the genomes of participants recruited for the CoMPaSS-NMD project using the innovative classification algorithm of gene variants named GORDIAN SCORE. The project aims at studying the genomes of individuals with neuromuscular disorders to identify pathways involved in the pathogenesis of the disease. The genomic analysis will be combined with clinical, histological, and MRI data. This approach is essential for the development of personalized clinical interventions. The study lays the groundwork for precision medicine in muscle diseases and for understanding the pathogenic mechanisms involved.

Field: Medicine / 06/MEDS-16 Malattie odontostomatologiche

The use of post-extraction dental implants has more recently become established as a successful procedure, even in areas of high aesthetic importance. Long-term data on these techniques (at least 5 years post-surgery) remain relatively limited.
